title: A threshold phenomenon for embeddings of Euclidean snowflakes and impossibility of dimension reduction
summary: Fix $0 1$, and this dimension bound is optimal as $k\to \infty$ up to lower order factors. We deduce from this statement that if $2<p<\infty$, then there exist arbitrarily large $n$-point subsets of $\ell_p$ with the property that if they embed with distortion $O(1)$ into $\ell_p^m$, then necessarily $m\gtrsim_p ((\log n)/(\log\log n)^2)^{p/2}$, thus demonstrating that the statement of the Johnson--Lindenstrauss dimension reduction lemma fails to hold for $\ell_p$
